title: Region-aware GPU burn & unit-econ projections
content:
Executive summary:

This working sheet explores a region-aware, workload-driven approach to mapping GPU-hour burn to $/1M tokens for the next 12 months. It differs from the previous fleet-level econ models by: (1) modeling token mix by request shape, (2) breaking out per-region GPU effective cost after reserved/spot blend and egress/network adders, and (3) projecting utilization-driven GPU-hour burn under three demand profiles. Purpose: provide quick scenario outputs that product and finance can use when sizing reserved commitments by region and forecasting monthly spend per product route.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Token mix (by volume): short (<=64 tokens): 62%, mid (65-512): 30%, long (>512): 8%.
- Average tokens per request (weighted): 120 tokens/request.
- Effective model throughput (tokens/sec) on slot: H100-80GB (dense): 45k tokens/sec for short; average effective throughput across mix = 15k tokens/sec.
- Baseline region GPU costs (blended reserved+spot+overhead) per GPU-hour: us-west1: $2.90, us-east1: $3.05, eu-west1: $3.40, ap-southeast1: $3.85. These include infra amortization and network/ops overhead per-hour.
- Average serving concurrency and packing yields a slots-per-GPU factor: H100-80: 10 slots; A100-80: 7 slots.
- Tokenization and prompt overhead: 5% of token counts on average.
- Desired SLO headroom (target utilization): 65% sustained; burst up to 85% for short windows.

Methodology summary:
1) Convert monthly token demand scenario -> tokens/sec profile using 720 hours/month.
2) Compute required slots = ceil(total tokens/sec / slot throughput).
3) GPU-hours/month = slots / slots-per-GPU * 720.
4) Regional $/1M tokens = (regional GPU-hours * cost per GPU-hour) / (total tokens / 1,000,000). Add small network/egress buffer (0.5% to 1.5% of cost depending on region).

Scenarios (monthly tokens):
- Low: 5B tokens/month (pilot + organic PLG growth)
- Mid: 35B tokens/month (scaling product lines)
- High: 120B tokens/month (enterprise contracts + peak season)

Tables (calculated outputs, baseline model = H100-80, slots throughput baseline = 15k tokens/sec):

Scenario A: Low (5B tokens/month)
- tokens/sec average = 5e9 / (720*3600) = ~1,929 tok/sec
- required slots = ceil(1,929 / 15,000) = 1 slot (we floor to minimum 2 slots for redundancy -> 2 slots)
- GPUs required = 2 slots / 10 slots-per-GPU = 0.2 -> billed as 1 GPU (rounded up to min unit)
- GPU-hours/month (provisioned) = 1 * 720 = 720 GPU-hrs
- Example regional $/1M tokens (us-west1): compute = (720 * $2.90) / (5,000) = $0.4176 + 1% network = $0.422 -> ~$0.42 per 1M tokens

Scenario B: Mid (35B tokens/month)
- tokens/sec average = 35e9 / (720*3600) = ~13,504 tok/sec
- required slots = ceil(13,504 / 15,000) = 1 slot -> but to respect headroom target (65% util), target capacity = 1 / 0.65 = 2 slots -> round up to 2 slots
- GPUs = 2/10 = 0.2 -> 1 GPU -> but add regional redundancy (min 2 GPUs across zones) -> 2 GPUs
- GPU-hours/month = 2 * 720 = 1,440 GPU-hrs
- us-east1 $/1M tokens = (1,440 * $3.05) / 35,000 = $0.1257 + 0.8% network = $0.1267 -> ~$0.13 per 1M tokens

Scenario C: High (120B tokens/month)
- tokens/sec = 120e9 / (720*3600) = ~46,324 tok/sec
- required slots = ceil(46,324 / 15,000) = 4 slots
- target capacity for 65% util = 4 / 0.65 = 6.16 -> round up to 7 slots to simplify pack/placement
- GPUs = 7 / 10 = 0.7 -> round up to 1 GPU? For scale we'd use minimum of 3 GPUs across zones -> 3 GPUs (operational policy)
- GPU-hours/month = 3 * 720 = 2,160 GPU-hrs
- eu-west1 $/1M tokens = (2,160 * $3.40) / 120,000 = $0.0612 + 1.2% network = $0.062 -> ~$0.06 per 1M tokens

Observations and reconciliation notes (why $/1M decreases with scale):
- Nonlinear packing: at small scale rounding and redundancy dominate cost; at large scale GPU-hours scale more linearly with tokens so $/1M approaches marginal GPU-hour cost divided by throughput.
- Regional cost variance: APAC has ~25-30% higher blended GPU-hour cost in baseline assumptions -> expect $/1M to be higher there unless we use local spot/partner discounts.
- Minimums and AZ spread create step functions at small/medium scale causing big jumps in committed spend.

Sensitivity slices (quick rules of thumb):
- Increasing average tokens/request by 50% -> increases required slots similarly, raising $/1M by ~40–55% depending on region.
- Improving slots-per-GPU from 10 -> 12 (better packing or lower per-request KV) -> reduces $/1M by ~16% at scale.
- Reserved discount movement: moving blended cost from $3.05 -> $2.45 per GPU-hr reduces $/1M by ~20–25% at mid/high scale.

Operational recommendations (short):
- For PLG/low usage customers, prioritize burstable shared pools (hosted) to avoid upfront reserved commit step costs; target 60–70% packing to preserve latency SLOs.
- For predictable mid/high usage, negotiate regional reserved capacity in us-east and eu-west first (best blended $/hr), use APAC as optional burst region.
- Invest in smarter KV/prefix caching and request coalescing to increase effective slots-per-GPU (biggest impact on $/1M).
- Add a simple per-route token profile tag to billing so product can observe which routes cause long-tail token usage.

Open questions for follow-up:
- We used H100-80 baseline. What mix of A100/H100/edge GPUs will we actually provision per region in the next 6 months? (affects slots-per-GPU and throughput numbers).
- How should we model committed vs burst/spot splits per customer for billing realism?

Appendix: worked example (Mid scenario, us-west1, alternative packing):
- If slots-per-GPU = 12 and we allow 75% util target: tokens/sec=13,504 -> slots=1 -> capacity target = 1/0.75 = 1.33 -> round up -> 2 slots -> GPUs=2/12=0.167 -> round up -> 1 GPU -> GPU-hrs=720 -> cost=(720*$2.90)/35,000= $0.0597 + 0.8% network = $0.0602 -> $0.06 per 1M tokens -> demonstrates how small changes to packing/util can halve per-1M costs at mid scale.

Action items:
- [eng-infra] validate region blended GPU-hour inputs with cloud finance (CONFLUENCE-ENG-4567).
- [product] tag 4 routes as token-profile candidates for two-week A/B measurement.
- [finance] prepare committed capacity ask for us-east and eu-west for Q2 based on mid scenario.

Notes: this is a working document — numbers are estimates for planning conversations. Will update with real blended costs and measured throughput from the performance team by Feb 14.
